incidents.victim: Ukrainian organizations using Dahua surveillance cameras (government and military)
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited Dahua's Easy4IP cloud remote-access feature, guessing predictable device serial numbers and weak credentials or unpatched firmware (CVE-2021-33044, CVE-2021-33045) to reach internet-connected cameras.
incidents.impact: Ukraine's CERT-UA found hackers had accessed surveillance cameras and recorders, exposing video feeds, changing settings, and creating unauthorized accounts; related activity has compromised over 14,500 Dahua devices in Ukraine and Russia since summer.

incidents.victim: 850+ compromised GitHub accounts across thousands of developer repositories
incidents.vector: Attackers used GitHub tokens stolen via infostealer malware and prior supply-chain leaks to plant a malicious "sync-check" workflow that prints and exfiltrates repository secrets.
incidents.impact: The campaign, dubbed "Gheist" by Wiz Research, created more than 13,500 malicious branches across 850+ compromised GitHub accounts, harvesting cloud credentials and secrets from personal and enterprise repositories.

incidents.victim: Node.js, .NET, Python, and other software using the Brotli compression library
incidents.vector: Unauthenticated out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decompression algorithm (CVE-2026-111497) lets attackers send malcrafted compressed data to corrupt server memory and execute code.
incidents.impact: Patches have rolled out across Node.js, Python Brotli bindings, Bun, Envoy, Istio, and .NET, with more downstream projects expected to confirm impact; researchers say the blast radius is broader than the recent PHP2Shell flaws.

incidents.vector: A threat actor used a master key accidentally exposed by LiteLLM in May to access the project's agent-hosting tooling and obtain a GitHub access token controlling LiteLLM's repositories.
incidents.impact: The attacker used repository control to distribute a version of the LiteLLM tool containing credential-harvesting malware, believed to have affected tens of thousands of users before discovery.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised customer accounts on the Andromeda cloud AI platform as part of a broader, industry-wide campaign against AI infrastructure providers.
incidents.impact: Intruders stole AI API keys and credentials from customer accounts, which are being rented out or sold on underground forums to provide unauthorized access to AI infrastructure.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached an internal CRM platform used by business partners to sell energy contracts for ENGIE's French gas supply business.
incidents.impact: ENGIE is notifying affected customers of the breach of partner-facing systems used to manage energy contracts.

incidents.vector: An intruder gained access to internal business systems through a learning management system and a customer relationship management platform.
incidents.impact: Genesys says it found no evidence the attacker pivoted from internal systems to its public-facing customer clouds.

incidents.vector: Attackers used an infinite-mint smart-contract exploit to create tokens outside the project's intended supply controls.
incidents.impact: The exploit allowed attackers to create and steal approximately $2.7 million worth of tokens from the Initia crypto project.

incidents.victim: eMudhra Limited (certificate authority) and relying websites/services
incidents.vector: A flaw in eMudhra's April 2025 intermediate-CA key-generation process produced private keys with insufficient randomness, allowing them to be derived from the public certificates.
incidents.impact: Eight compromised intermediate CA certificates could let attackers forge trusted TLS and code-signing certificates to impersonate websites or intercept traffic; major browser and OS vendors have revoked trust in the affected CAs and eMudhra has revoked the certificates.

incidents.victim: Websites and applications running PHP worldwide
incidents.vector: Two unauthenticated remote-code-execution vulnerabilities in PHP core (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619, dubbed "PHP2Shell") let attackers execute arbitrary commands on servers running vulnerable PHP versions via a plain HTTP request.
incidents.impact: The flaws caused government website outages in Europe and elsewhere; Cloudflare and others detected active exploitation, though researchers note a fully reliable exploit remains technically difficult to build.

incidents.victim: 600+ organizations across the Americas, Europe, and Australia in multiple critical infrastructure sectors
incidents.vector: SafePay actors gain initial access via compromised credentials and known vulnerabilities in internet-facing VPN devices, then use legitimate IT tools to move laterally and disable backups before exfiltrating data and encrypting systems.
incidents.impact: A joint CISA/FBI/USSS advisory warns SafePay has become one of the most active ransomware operations of 2026, extorting victims by threatening to leak stolen data and in some cases calling victims directly.

incidents.victim: Small number of Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC) staff devices
incidents.vector: Malicious ads served by an Israeli ad-tech company delivered zero-click spyware to a small number of staff devices.
incidents.impact: ABC wiped the affected devices as a precaution; the company says it found no confirmed signs of compromise.

incidents.victim: Unpatched PAN-OS GlobalProtect devices across multiple organizations
incidents.vector: Ransomware operators, including groups known as Qilin, Inc, and actors using Settra ransomware, are attempting to exploit an authentication-bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-0257) in PAN-OS GlobalProtect portal/gateway components patched since May 2026.
incidents.impact: Palo Alto Networks has observed limited successful exploit attempts against devices that remain unpatched or lack recommended mitigations in place.

incidents.victim: A small number of BeyondTrust Remote Support customers
incidents.vector: A China-linked actor exploited a critical authentication-bypass zero-day (CVE-2026-102764) in self-hosted BeyondTrust Remote Support appliances to gain initial access, establish persistence, escalate privileges, and move laterally.
incidents.impact: CISA added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog; BeyondTrust-hosted (SaaS) customers were already patched, while self-hosted appliance operators must apply the vendor patch.

incidents.victim: Telecommunications managed service provider and its clients' FortiGate firewalls
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a FortiManager vulnerability (CVE-2024-47575, "FortiJump") to register a rogue appliance, then used a second flaw (CVE-2025-61624) to deploy PEERSTITCH, a memory-resident implant that leaves no file on disk and blends into legitimate network traffic.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 found the attackers exfiltrated configuration and cryptographic material for more than 500 managed FortiGate firewalls protecting the provider's own network and its clients', and maintained long-term covert access; post-exploitation tradecraft overlapped with suspected nation-state intrusions.

incidents.victim: A limited number of Ivanti Connect Secure customers
incidents.vector: Threat actor UTA0576 chained three zero-day vulnerabilities in Ivanti Connect Secure to bypass authentication and remotely execute arbitrary commands.
incidents.impact: CISA added the actively exploited flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, enabling credential theft and data exfiltration on affected appliances.

incidents.vector: An opportunistic attacker used compromised credentials obtained through gaps in identity protections to make unauthorized VPN-based access attempts spanning several months.
incidents.impact: The bank's internal security team detected unusual activity and engaged Unit 42 to scope the intrusion, which resembled a stealthy espionage campaign but stemmed from basic security hygiene gaps rather than novel techniques.

incidents.victim: At least seven South Korean financial institutions
incidents.vector: A threat actor, suspected to be a Chinese-speaking operator, used an AI-assisted penetration-testing framework (ARTEX) alongside commercial AI coding tools to probe and compromise systems at multiple banks.
incidents.impact: South Korea's Financial Services Commission disclosed breaches exposing personal data belonging to at least 68,000 people across seven institutions, including theft of customer data and an outsourced developer's personal information.

incidents.vector: The ShinyHunters extortion group hacked the FBI's recruitment website, fbijobs.gov, and exfiltrated personnel records.
incidents.impact: Stolen data reportedly included FBI employees' medical and psychological records, Social Security numbers, home addresses, and unit/specialization details; attackers threatened to publish the files to pressure payment before the group's extortion site was taken down and a key suspect detained.
